titleStmt.title: Ovid, Amores 3.3: witness S — first-pass manuscript transcription
titleStmt.author: Publius Ovidius Naso

respStmt.resp: First-pass inspection of every extant verse image and manuscript encoding
respStmt.name: OpenAI Codex, encode_s agent

publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Awaiting independent second source reading; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 388, 389 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 48 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. Independent second reading remains required.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

interpretation.p: Notes are a first-reader evidence queue. Local uncertainty is documentation rather than an automatic user task. A different reader must independently inspect each verse and investigate all notes before integration.

div.head: First-pass encoding notes
div.note: A separate small E stands far left of the smaller-script remainder sse deos ...; the substantial horizontal space and smaller writing are retained without claiming a historical hand. The short group after deos is tentatively ine and remains unclear. The right inscription reads ad p̄iurā amicā, expanded periuram amicam. See opening and margin1 crops.
The source contracts Quā and n̄dū; the latter is expanded nondum. The displayed form retains the bars rather than silently supplying all letters.

A short marked sequence before numina is crossed out. It resembles nū and is locally unclear inside del. The deletion action is visible, but its exact letters and any earlier intended word are not reconstructed.
The witness repeats longa decensque and ends manet. Both que suspensions are retained; familiar alternative endings are not substituted.
The word after habuit appears radiauit, with u-like middle strokes; it remains locally unclear. The first pass does not silently normalize it to radiant.
The first contraction after Scilicet is represented ōne and expanded omne. The bar and merged minims should be checked independently; the source spelling of the following falsū is retained.
Crossed-p per and following que suspension are retained as a compound abbreviation. Both suos and illā are visible; source wording remains unchanged.
The group following At is represented cūs, with a bar; its expansion is not securely established. Meriti cur ego damna tuli is retained from visible letters without grammatical emendation.
The source spells cepheia and uses the suspension uobꝰ, expanded uobis. The final marked e is an est contraction.
A looped/crossed p-like abbreviation precedes male and is represented with a declared schematic pro sign. The source reads formosa iussa parente mori.

The opening tentatively reads Non sitis followed by a marked e. It is retained locally unclear and unexpanded rather than replaced from a familiar text. The later siue/sine distinction remains tentative; the final testes is adjacent to a dark physical blemish.
The word after mecū appears lusos, but its middle vowel remains tentative. The following irride multa deos is preserved without changing the word order.

The final contraction at the lower right is faded and represented p̄tis under unclear. The p̄iuri and p̄iuria suspensions are conventionally expanded; no complete missing word is supplied at the edge.

Actual manuscript389 begins here (viewer390). This page is pale and mottled throughout. The first and third words are tentatively Virgine and deceptore, locally marked unclear; final suo is visible. No alternate wording is imported.

The middle groups are faint and tentatively per nōn followed by marked d̄s ē. These remain locally unclear or unexpanded. The final feminaqꝫ tantū contractions are retained. The first reader does not resolve syntax by inventing letters.

Between forma and credulitate an uncertain short group looks ppos. It remains unclear without an unsupported conventional expansion. The clear surrounding words are retained despite overall page fading.
The source opening reads At tu sis followed by marked d̄s ē. Their relationship/expansions remain unspecified; the visible ceteras amat ille puellas is retained.
The manuscript reads Nobis flexibiles curuantur apollinis arcus. The faint page does not justify expanding this into missing text or replacing the witness wording.
The sequence after uiolat is tentatively focis and is locally unclear. The preceding pia and the inpūe contraction are retained rather than normalized to another construction.
The source begins Missaqꝫ and reads periuras tela ferire uetat. The que suspension is explicit.
The source spelling bacho and contracted pat̄ and opꝰ remain visible. The source is not normalized to Baccho in the reading display.
Repeated q̄qꝫ and h̄nt suspensions accompany oculos and pectꝰ; expansions preserve both parallel clauses without changing their written forms.
The word after ego is tentatively iurare. Its letter sequence remains locally unclear instead of being silently changed to another verbal form from a known edition.

The word before utere is suspended and represented moderatꝰ, expanded moderatius provisionally. The precise omitted ending should be checked from the mark. The first t̄m and illor̄ are conventional contractions.
The final verse reads Aut oculis certe parce puella meis. The next poem starts directly below it; those next-source words are boundary evidence only and are not included in3.3.
